cumulativeModel.note: Appendix C IS the cumulative ML3 set — every requirement that must hold at ML3 regardless of the level it first appeared. Nothing is marked ML3-only; cumulativeFrom records first appearance.
cumulativeModel.supersessionTrap: A naive union of the three appendices gives 152 and is WRONG. Exactly three ML1/ML2 requirements are REPLACED at ML3 (en dash in Appendix D's ML3 column) and are excluded here.

supersededAtML3.text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF software, and security products are applied within two weeks of release.
supersededAtML3.note: ML1/ML2 was a flat two weeks. ML3 splits into 48h (vendor-critical or working exploit) and two weeks. The two-week baseline does NOT tighten — the common vendor claim that ML3 moves this class 'from one month to two weeks' is wrong at both ends.

supersededAtML3.text: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within one month of release.
supersededAtML3.note: Unqualified one month becomes a 48h/one-month split.

supersededAtML3.text: Multi-factor authentication used for authenticating customers of online customer services provides a phishing-resistant option.
supersededAtML3.note: ML2 requires an option be OFFERED; ML3 requires it BE phishing-resistant. Letting a customer choose SMS passes ML2 and fails ML3.

scopeVerdict.headline: A code-generation harness cannot hold an Essential Eight Maturity Level Three rating, and neither can the applications it generates. Shipping a release that claims 'ML3' would be a false compliance claim.
reasons: Maturity is a property of an ORGANISATION'S SYSTEM, not a product. Every ASD artefact attaches it to an organisation or system owner; the assessment outcome vocabulary is 'The organisation is effectively meeting the control's objective'. There is no ASD mechanism by which a product, template or generator holds a maturity level, no approved-product list, and no ASD certification for anyone.

ASD's own SaaS adaptation disclaims it: the Small business cloud security guides state they 'are not designed to help an organisation reach a particular maturity level' and are 'an adaptation of the Essential Eight, rather than a strict Essential Eight implementation'.

Assessment is all-or-nothing and must be done as a package: every control in a strategy must be 'effective' or 'alternate control'; one ineffective control kills the strategy; one failed strategy kills the target level. 46 of 149 requirements are flatly unreachable by any codebase, which forecloses ML3 on the package rule alone.

Risk-accepting an entire strategy (or transferring it via cyber insurance) forces Maturity Level Zero for that strategy AND for the whole implementation. 'Restrict Microsoft Office macros' has zero reachable requirements in this stack, so a repo-scoped claim collapses to ML0, not ML3.

The Essential Eight contains ZERO software-development controls. All 108 controls in ISM Guidelines for software development and all 13 in Guidelines for database systems are tagged 'Essential 8: N/A'. Code quality cannot earn E8 maturity.

'Analogue' is not an ASD outcome. ASD's outcomes are Effective, Alternate control, Ineffective, Not applicable, No visibility, Not implemented, Not assessed. An alternate control must be demonstrated BY THE SYSTEM OWNER to give equivalent protection to the specific requirement — a per-system human judgement, not pre-earned credit a generator ships.

coverage.caveat: Computed from the rows below, not asserted. Even the 29 direct rows evidence a DEPLOYED INSTANCE operated by a customer organisation — a generated app that has never been deployed, backed up, or run an audit log in production evidences none of them.

scopeVerdict.honestClaim: Two strategies are genuinely tractable: Patch applications (8 direct — the lockfile plus deployment records ARE a software inventory with machine-readable install dates) and Regular backups (3 direct, 0 org-only — backups of a cloud app are entirely a property of its own infrastructure). MFA and Restrict administrative privileges are partially tractable for the app's own end users and privileged surfaces. Restrict Microsoft Office macros is 0% tractable. User application hardening and Patch operating systems are near 0% — they name Internet Explorer, Office ASR rules, Adobe Reader, .NET Framework, PowerShell, drivers and firmware by product. DEFENSIBLE CLAIM: 'generates applications that produce machine-checkable evidence for the software-supply-chain, application-audit-log, authentication and backup portions of an organisation's ML3 assessment, and hands the endpoint, driver, firmware, Office, browser-fleet, workstation-telemetry and incident-response portions to the organisation.' INDEFENSIBLE CLAIM: 'achieves ML3'.
scopeVerdict.betterFramework: The instrument ASD designed for a cloud/SaaS product is the ISM, assessed via IRAP. ISM Guidelines for software development (June 2026) holds the controls a generator can bake in and prove: ISM-0401 Secure by Design, ISM-2042 Secure by Default, ISM-1730 SBOM, ISM-2083 cryptographic BOM, ISM-2056 build provenance, ISM-2030 commit-time secret scanning, ISM-2032 zero-warning build gate, ISM-0402 SAST/DAST/SCA, ISM-0971 OWASP ASVS, ISM-1922 OWASP MASVS, ISM-1424 CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options, ISM-2063–2067 session handling, ISM-1276 parameterised queries, ISM-1268 least privilege via roles/views, ISM-1537 database security event logging, ISM-1717 security.txt. All are 'Essential 8: N/A' and all are shippable defaults.
scopeVerdict.currencyWarning: ASD opened consultation on 15 Jun 2026 to replace the Essential Eight with an ISM-grounded 'Essentials series' ('Essentials for enterprise IT' first), citing the cloud gap explicitly; reported deprecation ~12 months, retirement ~24 months. Any E8 positioning built now has roughly a two-year shelf life, and the stated reason for the change is precisely the mismatch this register documents.
assessorTraps: Documentation and interviews are ASD's WEAKEST evidence tier ('Poor evidence'); testing with simulated activity is 'Excellent'. A committed policy file proves almost nothing; a CI job that attempts the prohibited action and asserts denial proves a lot.
Exceptions need formal approval, eight documented elements, and 'should not be approved beyond one year'.
ASD sets NO numeric window for 'in a timely manner' or 'as soon as possible'. Do not invent 24/48/72h SLAs — that creates a contractual obligation with no framework backing.

appliesToWebApp.direct: Satisfiable by an artefact in or produced by the repo or its deployed system, with no reinterpretation of the asset class ASD names. Still evidences a deployed instance, not the generator.
appliesToWebApp.analogue: ASD's named asset class does not exist in a Next.js + Expo + Supabase deployment, but a same-intent, machine-checkable control does. NOT an ASD outcome — an assessor must accept it as an 'alternate control' and may refuse.
appliesToWebApp.org-only: No honest counterpart. Marked org-only rather than analogue wherever the nearest mapping is already claimed under another requirement, because double-counting one artefact across rows is the commonest form of compliance inflation.

fieldSemantics.evidenceIfDirect: Populated only for direct rows; names a file, CI check, database policy, HTTP header or log stream. For analogue rows the proposed artefact sits inside why.
fieldSemantics.orgOnlyResidue: Named asset classes inside a partially-reachable requirement that no repository can reach and the organisation must evidence regardless.
fieldSemantics.sharedClause: Non-empty where ASD repeats identical text across strategies. All instances carry IDENTICAL classification, timeframe and evidence here — the source research classified three of these clauses four different ways across four strategies, which is corrected. The evidence is ONE artefact and must be counted once.
fieldSemantics.ismControls: From the October 2024 E8-to-ISM mapping. Empty arrays are attribution gaps in this register (chiefly Restrict administrative privileges and the Patch operating systems scanning/patching rows), not gaps in ASD's mapping; fill from the mapping XLSX before using for ISM traceability.

Event logs from internet-facing servers are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.
Event logs from non-internet-facing servers are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.
Event logs from workstations are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

Same ASD sentence, contradictory verdicts.
